title: Numerical investigation of a rotor blade tip vortex pair
author: Brendon Loiola Messali
abstract: With the increasing energy demand around the planet and growing interest in environmental preservation, new forms of electrical power generation have been adopted, including wind energy. In the quest to reduce environmental impact, renewable energy sources are being preferred over traditional sources, such as oil burning. However, wind energy, despite being a renewable source, can still cause environmental pollution, mainly in the form of noise pollution, due to the noise generated by turbine blades. Just as with aircraft flying over urban areas, wind turbines require a minimum distance from the nearest dwellings to minimize the impact on people's lives. Therefore, various studies are being conducted to enable the reduction of noise generated by these turbines. In this work, two central experiments on the topic are analyzed, both focused on investigating the tip vortex. From the attempt to simulate a blade tip device for a rotor, a methodology for anisotropic numerical simulation is presented, which is tested in a fixed wing test case.
